extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers, journal editors, authors, and the healthcare evidence-synthesis community
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and expectations for performing peer review for JBI journals and contributing to trustworthy healthcare evidence syntheses; highlights qualities, challenges, and the role of technology and reviewer training. Focused on what makes effective peer review in the context of evidence synthesis and healthcare publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time, expertise and dedication
rubrics_metrics.description: At JBI we rely on the time, expertise and dedication of peer reviewers to help us provide the highest quality evidence-based resources for healthcare globally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer reviewers must be willing to volunteer sufficient time and apply their subject-matter expertise and dedication so journals can maintain high-quality outputs (JBI EBP Database and JBI journals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong peer review skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers who possess strong peer review skills are needed to support the editorial process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors face challenges in finding reviewers who both have strong reviewing skills and the time to commit; strong skills include the ability to critically evaluate methodology, reporting, and relevance in evidence syntheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to help authors strengthen their work / produce trustworthy evidence syntheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers help authors strengthen their work to produce trustworthy evidence syntheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A key evaluative role of reviewers is to provide constructive feedback that improves rigour, clarity, and trustworthiness of manuscripts submitted to evidence synthesis journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to research integrity and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Research integrity and transparency are paramount in the peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should prioritize practices that uphold integrity and transparency when assessing manuscripts and when engaging with innovations such as AI-assisted review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper calibration of AI and adequate reviewer training
rubrics_metrics.description: Proper calibration of AI and adequate training of peer reviewers will help overcome barriers, enhancing the practice of academic publishing and the capacity of peer reviewers to participate meaningfully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When technology (AI) is used in peer review, it must be carefully calibrated and reviewers must receive training to use it responsibly; this is framed as a solution to skill/time shortages and a means to enhance review quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance optimism with caution about technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Be optimistic, and also cautious, about the advancements technology can offer in the peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While innovation and technological tools may improve processes, reviewers and editors should be cautious about unintended consequences and ensure technology supports — not undermines — integrity and quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary generosity and service to the scholarly community
rubrics_metrics.description: Exceptional peer reviewers generously volunteer their time and expertise to help authors improve their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The voluntary nature of peer review is emphasized; recognizing and appreciating reviewers' contributions supports continued participation and high standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to maintaining the highest standards of quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers are expected to commit to maintaining the highest standards of quality in published research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers' contributions are framed as essential to preserving evidence-based resources and the overall quality of journal content; this underpins selection and recognition of outstanding reviewers.
